ap_biology-f01.title: Interpreting and evaluating results: fruit flies

stimulus.description: A researcher breeds populations of fruit flies for an increased number of bristles on the abdomen. In each generation only the flies with the most bristles were allowed to mate to produce the next generation. After different numbers of generations of selective breeding, the number of bristles per fly was counted in a sample of flies. Each measurement used n = 12 flies. Mean number of bristles per fly (bristles) ± 2SE for fruit flies at four levels of the independent variable; n = 12 for each level

columns: Mean number of bristles per fly (bristles) ± 2SE

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Explain how repeated selective breeding for a heritable trait can change the mean value of that trait in a population.
parts.model_answer: Only the individuals with the desired heritable variation reproduce, so the alleles for that trait become more frequent in each generation and the population mean shifts.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives a correct explanation or description of the biological concept
required_elements: Only individuals with the selected heritable trait reproduce, so the alleles for the trait become more frequent in each generation
alt_solutions: the breeder chooses the parents, so the trait-related alleles increase in the next generation
selection for the trait passes the favored alleles to more offspring, shifting the mean
common_errors: says the flies change their bristles during their lifetime in order to pass the change on
says selective breeding creates the needed alleles because the flies need them
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: (i) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in the investigation. (ii) Identify one factor that should be kept constant so the results are due to the independent variable. (iii) Describe the pattern in the data in the table.
parts.model_answer: (i) Independent variable: number of generations of selective breeding; dependent variable: number of bristles per fly. (ii) For example temperature. (iii) The mean number of bristles per fly increases as the independent variable increases, from 34.0 to 52.5.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies both the independent variable and the dependent variable
required_elements: The independent variable is number of generations of selective breeding and the dependent variable is number of bristles per fly
alt_solutions: manipulated variable: number of generations of selective breeding; measured response: number of bristles per fly
changes number of generations of selective breeding and measures number of bristles per fly
common_errors: names the dependent variable as the independent variable
names only one of the two variables
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies a valid factor that is kept constant
required_elements: Names a factor other than the independent variable that is held the same in all treatments
alt_solutions: temperature
the food supplied to the cultures
the number of flies in each culture bottle
common_errors: names the independent variable as the constant
names a factor that was changed between treatments
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes the pattern in the data, using values from the table
required_elements: States that the mean number of bristles per fly increases as the independent variable increases, citing values
alt_solutions: the number of bristles per fly goes up from 34.0 to 52.5
the values increase across the levels, citing the first and last means
common_errors: describes the opposite trend
describes the pattern without any values from the table
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: (i) Calculate the percent change in the mean number of bristles per fly from the lowest level to the highest level of the independent variable. Show your work. (ii) Using the ±2SE values, determine whether the difference between the mean at 3 and the mean at 6 is statistically supported, and justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: (i) percent change = (52.5 - 34.0) / 34.0 x 100 = 54.4%. (ii) 3: 34.32 to 39.68; 6: 42.84 to 48.36. The ranges do not overlap, so the difference between the two treatments is statistically supported.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets up the percent change with the correct formula and values (expression)
required_elements: Uses (final - initial) / initial x 100 with the values 52.5 and 34.0
alt_solutions: percent change = difference divided by the starting value times 100
common_errors: divides by the final value instead of the initial value
forgets to multiply by 100
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the correct percent change (answer)
common_errors: uses the wrong values from the table or an incorrect formula
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: States whether the difference is supported and justifies it by comparing the ±2SE ranges
required_elements: The ±2SE ranges do not overlap, so the difference is supported
alt_solutions: compares the mean ± 2SE intervals of the two treatments and states the conclusion
separated error ranges mean the difference is unlikely to be due to chance
common_errors: compares only the means
states the wrong conclusion for the ranges
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Predict the mean number of bristles after 9 generations if the researcher had instead allowed the flies to mate at random with no selection by the researcher, and justify your prediction.
parts.model_answer: The mean number of bristles would stay close to the starting value (about 35). Without selection for high bristle number, flies with many and with few bristles reproduce equally, so the frequencies of the alleles for the trait are not systematically changed.

rubric_rows.criterion: Makes a reasonable prediction
required_elements: The mean number of bristles would stay close to the starting value and would not increase substantially
alt_solutions: there would be little change in the mean from generation 0
the mean would remain about the same as at the beginning

predicts that the mean would fall to zero
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies the prediction with biological reasoning
required_elements: Without selection the frequencies of the alleles for the trait are not systematically changed from one generation to the next
alt_solutions: flies with different bristle numbers reproduce about equally, so there is no consistent shift

gives no reason based on alleles or reproduction

The activity of the enzyme beta-galactosidase, which is encoded by a gene of the lac operon, was measured in samples of the cells. Each measurement used n = 6 cultures. Mean beta-galactosidase activity (units of enzyme activity) ± 2SE for bacteria at four levels of the independent variable; n = 6 for each level

columns: Mean beta-galactosidase activity (units of enzyme activity) ± 2SE

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe how the presence of lactose in the medium leads to transcription of the genes of the lac operon in E. coli.
parts.model_answer: A lactose derivative binds to the repressor protein, which then releases the operator, so RNA polymerase can transcribe the genes of the operon.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives a correct explanation or description of the biological concept
required_elements: A lactose derivative binds the repressor, which releases the operator so RNA polymerase can transcribe the genes
alt_solutions: lactose inactivates the repressor, so the operator is no longer blocked and the genes are transcribed
binding of the inducer to the repressor frees the operator for transcription
common_errors: says lactose binds directly to the DNA and makes the genes replicate
says the repressor is destroyed by the cell when lactose is absent
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: (i) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in the investigation. (ii) Identify one factor that should be kept constant so the results are due to the independent variable. (iii) Describe the pattern in the data in the table.
parts.model_answer: (i) Independent variable: concentration of lactose; dependent variable: beta-galactosidase activity. (ii) For example temperature. (iii) The mean beta-galactosidase activity increases as the independent variable increases, from 1.9 to 86.2.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies both the independent variable and the dependent variable
required_elements: The independent variable is concentration of lactose and the dependent variable is beta-galactosidase activity
alt_solutions: manipulated variable: concentration of lactose; measured response: beta-galactosidase activity
changes concentration of lactose and measures beta-galactosidase activity
common_errors: names the dependent variable as the independent variable
names only one of the two variables
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies a valid factor that is kept constant
required_elements: Names a factor other than the independent variable that is held the same in all treatments
alt_solutions: temperature
the type of growth medium other than lactose
the starting number of bacterial cells
common_errors: names the independent variable as the constant
names a factor that was changed between treatments
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes the pattern in the data, using values from the table
required_elements: States that the mean beta-galactosidase activity increases as the independent variable increases, citing values
alt_solutions: the beta-galactosidase activity goes up from 1.9 to 86.2
the values increase across the levels, citing the first and last means
common_errors: describes the opposite trend
describes the pattern without any values from the table
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: (i) Calculate the percent change in the mean beta-galactosidase activity from the lowest level to the highest level of the independent variable. Show your work. (ii) Using the ±2SE values, determine whether the difference between the mean at 0.1 and the mean at 0.5 is statistically supported, and justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: (i) percent change = (86.2 - 1.9) / 1.9 x 100 = 4436.8%. (ii) 0.1: 10.42 to 13.18; 0.5: 35.24 to 40.36. The ranges do not overlap, so the difference between the two treatments is statistically supported.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets up the percent change with the correct formula and values (expression)
required_elements: Uses (final - initial) / initial x 100 with the values 86.2 and 1.9
alt_solutions: percent change = difference divided by the starting value times 100
common_errors: divides by the final value instead of the initial value
forgets to multiply by 100
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the correct percent change (answer)
common_errors: uses the wrong values from the table or an incorrect formula
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: States whether the difference is supported and justifies it by comparing the ±2SE ranges
required_elements: The ±2SE ranges do not overlap, so the difference is supported

common_errors: compares only the means

rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Predict how the enzyme activity in a mutant strain whose repressor cannot bind to the operator would compare with the activity of the original strain in a medium without lactose, and justify your prediction.

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies the prediction with biological reasoning

stimulus.description: A researcher exposes cultured liver cells to different concentrations of a hormone that binds to a receptor on the cell surface. The researcher measures the amount of a response molecule that the cells produce in the signal transduction pathway. The table shows the data.

parts.prompt: Describe how binding of a hormone to a receptor on the surface of a cell can lead to a change in the activity of the cell.
parts.model_answer: Binding of the hormone changes the receptor, which starts a signal transduction pathway of relay molecules that produces a cellular response.

parts.label: B

parts.model_answer: (i) rate = (53.3 - 40) / (8 - 2) = 2.22 µM per nM. (ii) The graph levels off at about 59.1 µM, which estimates the maximum.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the correct average rate of increase with units (answer)
common_errors: uses the wrong values from the table or an incorrect formula
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

A researcher marks equal numbers of green and brown beetles, releases them in plots of green grass, and counts the number of marked beetles of each color that are alive after five days. Birds that hunt by sight eat the beetles.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe the conditions that must be met for natural selection to occur in a population.
parts.model_answer: There must be heritable variation in a trait, and individuals with some versions of the trait must survive and reproduce more than others.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives a correct description of the biological concept or process
required_elements: There is heritable variation in a trait, and some variants survive and reproduce more than others
alt_solutions: individuals differ in an inherited trait that affects survival or reproduction
differential reproductive success of heritable variants
common_errors: says individuals change their traits when the environment requires it
says that natural selection occurs without any variation among individuals
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify one factor that should be kept the same for the green beetles and the brown beetles, and explain why.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies an appropriate feature of the experimental design and gives the reason

rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Predict whether more green beetles or more brown beetles will be alive after five days.
parts.model_answer: More green beetles than brown beetles will be alive.

rubric_rows.criterion: Makes an appropriate prediction of the results
required_elements: Predicts that more green beetles than brown beetles survive
alt_solutions: the green beetles will survive better in the green grass
fewer brown beetles will be alive after five days
common_errors: predicts that more brown beetles will survive
predicts equal survival of the two colors with no reason
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Justify your prediction in terms of natural selection.

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies the prediction or result with biological reasoning

ap_biology-f09.title: A mutation that prevents crossing over

stimulus.description: A researcher studies meiosis in the cells of an organism with two pairs of homologous chromosomes. A mutation in some of the organism's cells prevents the homologous chromosomes from forming the tetrads in prophase I, so crossing over does not occur in these cells. Meiosis in these cells is otherwise normal.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe what happens during crossing over in prophase I of meiosis.
parts.model_answer: Homologous chromosomes pair up and exchange segments of DNA between nonsister chromatids.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives a correct description of the biological concept or process
required_elements: Homologous chromosomes pair and exchange segments between nonsister chromatids
alt_solutions: pieces of DNA are swapped between homologous chromosomes
the homologs trade sections of their chromatids
common_errors: says that sister chromatids exchange segments to make new alleles
says that whole chromosomes are exchanged between cells
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain how crossing over increases the genetic variation among the gametes produced by one individual.
parts.model_answer: Crossing over produces chromosomes with new combinations of the alleles that were on the two homologs, so the gametes carry combinations that neither parent chromosome had.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives a correct explanation of how or why the process works
required_elements: Crossing over creates chromosomes with new combinations of alleles, so gametes differ from the original chromosomes
alt_solutions: the exchange of segments recombines alleles that were on different homologs
new allele combinations on one chromosome are produced
common_errors: says crossing over creates new alleles that did not exist before
says crossing over changes the number of chromosomes in the gametes
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Predict the effect of the mutation on the genetic variation among the gametes produced by an individual whose cells have the mutation.
parts.model_answer: The genetic variation among the gametes will decrease.

required_elements: Predicts that the genetic variation among the gametes decreases
alt_solutions: fewer different allele combinations will be in the gametes

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Justify your prediction in terms of the combinations of alleles on the chromosomes.

ap_biology-f10.title: A population bottleneck

stimulus.description: A population of 5,000 ground squirrels is reduced to only 20 individuals by a disease that kills squirrels at random with respect to their alleles. The survivors reproduce, and over many generations the population grows back to 5,000 squirrels.

parts.prompt: Describe what is meant by genetic drift.
parts.model_answer: Genetic drift is a change in the allele frequencies of a population from one generation to the next that occurs by chance.

alt_solutions: allele frequencies change because of random events rather than selection

common_errors: says genetic drift is a change in allele frequency caused by the environment favoring certain alleles
says genetic drift is the movement of alleles between populations
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain why genetic drift has a larger effect on allele frequencies in a small population than in a large population.

parts.label: D

ap_biology-f13.title: Data analysis: percent of moths that survived

stimulus.description: The table shows the mean percent of moths that survived for three days ± 2SE after release onto tree trunks; n = 8 trunks for each group. Birds that hunt by sight feed on the moths.

columns: Mean percent of moths that survived (percent of moths) ± 2SE

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe the pattern shown by the data in the table, using values from the table to support your description.
parts.model_answer: The mean percent of moths that survived decreases across the levels: 66.0, 31.2, 28.7; it is greatest at Dark moths on dark bark.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes the pattern and supports it with values from the table
required_elements: Describes how the mean percent of moths that survived changes across the levels and names the level with the greatest mean using the table values
alt_solutions: goes down across the levels
falls from the first to the last level
common_errors: describes a pattern that the data do not show
describes the pattern without values from the table
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the percent change in the mean percent of moths that survived from Dark moths on dark bark to Dark moths on light bark. Show your work.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the correct percent change with the formula applied (answer)
common_errors: uses the wrong values from the table or an incorrect formula
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: A student claims that the mean percent of moths that survived at Dark moths on dark bark is greater than the mean at each of the other two levels. Using the ±2SE ranges in the table, evaluate whether the data support the claim.
parts.model_answer: The ±2SE ranges are Dark moths on dark bark: 61.96 to 70.04; Light moths on dark bark: 28.80 to 33.60; Dark moths on light bark: 26.62 to 30.78. The range at Dark moths on dark bark does not overlap the range at either of the other levels, so the data support the claim for both comparisons.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the ±2SE ranges of both comparisons to evaluate the claim

concludes that the claim is not supported even though the ranges do not overlap
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.prompt: Explain how the results illustrate natural selection acting on the color of the moths.
